alt: The butterfly heart design laser engraved as a grayscale relief on pale maple, with a diode laser head above it
scene: LASER ENGRAVED, NOT CARVED. The design from image 1 rendered as a LASER ENGRAVING on a flat, smooth panel of pale maple plywood about 25 by 20 cm: the surface is completely flat with no carved depth at all; instead the design appears as a photographic sepia-brown burn whose tone varies smoothly from pale untouched wood on the highest parts of the design to deep dark brown in the deepest parts, exactly like a grayscale depth map burned into wood, with crisp edges and a slightly satin sheen where the burn is darkest. The panel lies on the honeycomb bed of a small desktop diode laser engraver, plain and unbranded, with the laser module hanging a few centimetres above it and a faint wisp of smoke. Wide magazine shot, bright workshop light. The finish swatch applies only to the colour of bare maple and the warm brown of the burn.

alt: A printed grayscale depth map of the design on paper lying beside the finished laser engraving of it
scene: SIDE BY SIDE ON THE BENCH, shot from directly above. On the LEFT, a sheet of white paper printed with the design from image 1 as a pure GRAYSCALE DEPTH MAP: a black background, the raised parts of the design in pale grey to white, the lower parts in darker greys, no colour, no shading, no lines, just tone equals height, like a heightmap. On the RIGHT, the same design LASER ENGRAVED into a flat pale maple panel as a sepia burn whose darkness follows that map. The two match exactly in composition. A pencil and a small pair of calipers lie between them. Bright even light.

alt: The same design laser engraved on four materials: pale maple, figured walnut, black slate and tan leather
scene: FOUR SMALL SQUARES OF DIFFERENT MATERIALS IN A ROW, each about 10 cm, each laser engraved with the same design from image 1 as a flat tonal burn (no carved depth): far left, pale maple plywood where the burn reads cleanly in warm sepia; second, heavily figured walnut where the wild grain visibly fights the image and the design is harder to read; third, black slate where the engraving appears as pale grey-white against the dark stone; far right, tan full-grain leather where the burn is dark brown and crisp. Laid on the bench, shot from above, bright even light, a small laser-cut offcut beside them.

alt: Laser Studio poster: photos, 3D models and the night sky turned into ready-to-burn laser files on your own machine; 11 output styles, star maps, sundials, tumblers, boxes; 100 percent offline, one-time purchase
scene: COMPOSED: the owner's own Laser Studio marketing poster (MARKETING/POSTERS/poster_01.png); do not render.

alt: The relief design laser engraved as a grayscale burn on pale maple, lying beside the carved wooden version of the same design
scene: TWO MACHINES, ONE FILE. On the bench, side by side: LEFT, a flat panel of pale maple plywood on which the design from image 1 has been LASER ENGRAVED as a smooth sepia-brown tonal burn with no carved depth, like a photograph burned into wood. RIGHT, the same design carved in real relief in the house finish. Shot from directly above in bright even light so the two readings of one design can be compared. Nothing else in frame.
